sentences.text: The fossil skeleton contains numerous vertebrae, a complete left wing, and both hind limbs.
Preserved soft tissues include wing membranes, a membrane on the tibia, a neck mane, and foot webbing.
The animal had a wingspan of 1 meter and a body length of about 50 centimeters.
The fourth phalanx in the wing finger was naturally absent, a condition also seen in Nyctosaurus.
A 2005 study revealed many blood vessels in the wing membrane, suggesting a role in thermoregulation.
The genus Beipiaopterus was named in 2003 by the paleontologist Lü Junchang.
The generic name combines the city of Beipiao in Liaoning Province with the Greek word for wing.
The only known species is based on a crushed partial skeleton of a subadult that lacks a skull.
Lü classified the animal in the family Ctenochasmatidae based on elongated neck vertebrae and humerus shape.
This pterosaur lived during the Aptian stage of the Early Cretaceous in the Yixian Formation of China.
The animal lived between 125.77 and 119.57 million years ago, spanning the Barremian to Aptian stages.
A 2018 study placed the genus in a derived position within Ctenochasmatidae, contradicting earlier views of it being a basal member.
